Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the DORA Art. 24 digital operational resilience testing programme across every ICT system supporting a critical or important function (CIF); escalates untested CIF systems to the Chief Info Security Officer and the management body

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Arts. 24-25 read against the EUR-Lex consolidated text plus Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1774, re-read at each annual programme refresh; applies to the EU authorised entities only, with non-EU subsidiaries mapped separately and excluded from the DORA test calendar

In-scope processes.value: CIF identification and mapping -> risk-based annual test plan -> execution of the Art. 25(1) test types (vulnerability assessments and scans, open source analyses, network security assessments, gap analyses, physical security reviews, questionnaires and scanning software, source code reviews where feasible, scenario-based tests, compatibility, performance and end-to-end testing, penetration testing) -> finding remediation to closure and re-test

In-scope systems.value: Qualys/Tenable for vulnerability scanning and network security assessment; the CMDB supplies the CIF asset population; k6/Gatling and JMeter cover performance and end-to-end tests; the test calendar and findings live in the GRC platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: Digital Operational Resilience Testing Programme (DORTP) standard - CIF scoping rules, the Art. 25(1) test-type matrix per asset tier, risk-based frequency, tester independence rules under Art. 24(5), severity grading, remediation SLAs and the annual management-body reporting pack

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the management body on the recommendation of the Chief Info Security Officer; re-approved at least yearly and re-opened out of cycle after any major ICT-related incident or material change to a CIF architecture

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Art. 24(6) - every CIF-supporting ICT system carries at least one completed test per calendar year; the annual programme and results summary is tabled at the Q4 management body meeting; the Art. 26 threat-led penetration testing cycle (at least every 3 years) runs on a separate TLPT register

Deadline reminders configured.value: GRC platform test calendar raises owner alerts at T-60, T-30 and T-7 days against each system's annual test due date; any system past due appears on the CISO weekly overdue-test report until it is closed

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Scoping notes, test plans, raw findings, remediation tickets, re-test results and management body summaries retained 5 years from test completion and producible to the competent authority on request

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A CIF system that passes its annual due date untested, a test executed by a non-independent tester, and any critical finding past its remediation SLA are each raised as an ICT risk issue with either a dated remediation plan or a time-bound risk acceptance

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The CISO signs closure of every critical and high finding on a CIF-supporting system and personally approves any risk acceptance that leaves a CIF exposure open past its SLA

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All ICT systems and applications flagged as CIF-supporting in the CIF register for the calendar year, joined to every test execution recorded in the DORTP test calendar for that year

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Fail if any CIF-supporting system completed no Art. 25 test in the calendar year, if a test was executed by someone in the build or run team for that system, if the test type applied does not match the DORTP matrix for the asset tier, or if a critical finding sat open past its SLA with no approved risk acceptance; one or more fails escalates to the management body

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is at least annual per CIF system on a rolling programme, so assurance runs annually across the full-year population, with a half-year interim reconciliation of the test calendar to the CIF register to catch coverage drift before December

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: The auditor must not have scoped, executed, remediated or signed off any sampled test and must not report to the Operational Resilience Lead

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual DORTP assurance workpaper - CIF population extract, calendar reconciliation, sample re-performance notes, finding ageing analysis and exception log - filed in the compliance evidence repository under DORA/Art-24/<year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Testing programme standard, the annual test schedule with per-system completion dates, the summary of findings by severity and the remediation status report, packaged for the competent authority within 10 business days of a supervisory request

Regulator response path.value: The Operational Resilience Lead drafts the supervisory response, the Head of Compliance clears it and the Chief Info Security Officer signs it before it goes to the national competent authority; any statement about an untested CIF system is cleared by Legal Counsel first

checklist.step: Refresh the critical-or-important-function register and derive test scope
actions: Ask each business service owner to confirm which of their functions meet the Art. 3(22) test - a disruption would materially impair financial performance, soundness or the continuity of authorised services.
In the CMDB open Configuration ▸ Business Services and export every CI mapped to a confirmed CIF with CI class, environment, hosting model and the supporting ICT third-party provider.
Cross-check the export against the Register of Information contract list held by the Third-Party Risk Manager so outsourced components inside a CIF chain are not dropped.
Tier each CI (Tier 1 CIF-critical, Tier 2 CIF-supporting, Tier 3 out of scope) and record who confirmed it and on what date.
File the signed CIF register version as the scoping baseline for the year in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: a dated, owner-confirmed CIF register exists with every supporting CI tiered and reconciled to the Register of Information.

checklist.step: Set the Art. 25(1) test-type matrix for each asset tier
actions: List the Art. 25(1) test types down the rows - vulnerability assessment and scan, open source analysis, network security assessment, gap analysis, physical security review, questionnaire and scanning software, source code review where feasible, scenario-based test, compatibility test, performance test, end-to-end test, penetration test.
Set the minimum annual coverage per tier - Tier 1 takes scenario-based, performance, end-to-end and penetration testing; Tier 2 takes vulnerability, network and gap analysis as a floor.
Agree the matrix with the Chief Info Security Officer and the Vulnerability Management Lead / Security Engineering Lead so tooling capacity matches the demand it creates.
Publish the matrix as a versioned appendix to the DORTP standard in Confluence and quote its version number on every test plan.
checklist.done: a versioned test-type matrix maps each asset tier to a named minimum set of Art. 25(1) test types.

checklist.step: Build the annual test calendar and load it into the GRC platform
actions: In the GRC platform open Risk ▸ Assessments and create one test record per CIF system per required test type, carrying CI id, tier, test type and matrix version.

Set each due date so no CIF-supporting system exceeds 12 months since its last completed test of that type, spreading load across quarters with the Vulnerability Management Lead / Security Engineering Lead.
Name a test owner, an executing tester and an accountable system owner on every record; a blank owner blocks calendar publication.
Configure T-60, T-30 and T-7 day notifications and a weekly overdue report routed to the Chief Info Security Officer.
Publish the calendar to the Chief Information Officer and the business service owners and log their acknowledgement.
checklist.done: every CIF system has dated, owned test records in the GRC platform with reminders armed and no gap longer than 12 months.

checklist.step: Confirm tester independence before any test is commissioned
actions: For each scheduled test check the named tester sits outside the build and run teams for the system under test, as Art. 24(5) requires.
Pull the tester's entitlements to the target CI from the IAM platform and confirm they hold no developer, administrator or change-approver rights.
Where an external tester is used, verify the firm's professional indemnity cover and quote its contract id from the CLM repository on the test record.
Reassign any test where independence cannot be evidenced rather than letting the system team test itself.
checklist.done: every scheduled test names a tester whose independence is evidenced from entitlement data or an external engagement contract.

checklist.step: Scope and brief each individual test before execution
actions: Draft the test plan from the DORTP template covering objective, in-scope CIs and interfaces, test type, environment, data handling, rules of engagement, escalation contact and stop conditions.
Get the system owner to confirm production-equivalence of the test environment or, where production testing is required, attach the Change Coordinator's approved change record.
Write the pass criteria up front - recovery inside the agreed recovery time objective, no unauthenticated path to CIF data, throughput sustained at 1.5x observed peak.
Notify the SOC Lead of the window so live testing is not handled as an intrusion, and record the notification date.
Attach the approved plan to the GRC test record before execution starts.
checklist.done: each test has an approved, pre-notified plan with explicit pass criteria attached to its GRC record.

checklist.step: Run vulnerability and network security assessments on the CIF estate
actions: In Qualys/Tenable build a scan target group from the CIF CI list exported from the CMDB and confirm asset coverage is at least 98 percent of that list before launching.
Run authenticated scans against the CIF hosts plus an external attack-surface scan of the internet-facing CIF endpoints.
Export findings with CVE id, CVSS base score, affected CI, first-seen date and the available fix.
Reconcile the scanned asset count back to the CMDB CIF list and take every unscanned CI to the Infrastructure / Network Engineer rather than excluding it.
Attach the scan report and the coverage reconciliation to the GRC test record.
checklist.done: authenticated and external scans cover the CIF asset list and every unscanned CI has a documented reason and a re-scan date.

checklist.step: Run performance, capacity and end-to-end tests on Tier 1 CIF chains
actions: Take the observed annual peak transaction volumes for the CIF from the Capacity Planner and build a k6/Gatling scenario at 1.5x that peak.
Execute the load against the full end-to-end chain including third-party components, not just the internal application tier.
Record 95th and 99th percentile response times, error rates and the load at which the chain degrades, against the pass criteria in the plan.
Where the chain breaches its recovery time or throughput objective, raise a finding and tell the system owner and the Business Continuity Manager the same day.
File the run output and the Grafana dashboard capture on the GRC test record.
checklist.done: each Tier 1 CIF chain has a dated load result at 1.5x peak with percentile latencies and a pass or fail against its stated objective.

checklist.step: Run scenario-based tests against severe-but-plausible disruption scenarios
actions: Select scenarios from the ICT risk register - loss of a primary data centre or cloud region, ransomware encryption of a CIF data store, failure of a critical ICT third-party provider, corruption of a golden-source data set.
Run each scenario with the Incident Response Lead, the Disaster Recovery Engineer and the affected business service owner, timing every recovery step against the RTO and RPO.
Capture the actual recovery time, the data loss window and every manual workaround the team had to invent during the exercise.
Debrief within 5 business days and convert each gap into a GRC finding with a named owner.
Revise the ICT response and recovery plans with whatever the exercise proved wrong.
checklist.done: each selected scenario has a timed run, a measured recovery against RTO/RPO and gaps converted into owned findings.

checklist.step: Extend testing into ICT third-party components inside CIF chains
actions: From the Register of Information pull every provider supporting a CIF and open its contract in the CLM repository.
Check the contract carries the Art. 30(3) audit, access and inspection rights and the provider's obligation to participate in the entity's resilience testing.
Request from each provider its current independent assurance report (ISAE 3402 or SOC 2 Type II) and the penetration test summary covering the service actually consumed.
Where the provider will not test or share results, log the residual risk with the Chief Info Security Officer and raise a contract remediation action with the Contracts Manager.
Record per provider what was tested, by whom, when and with what result on the CIF test record.
checklist.done: every CIF-supporting provider has a current assurance artefact on file or a logged residual risk with a contract remediation action.

checklist.step: Grade and log every finding with severity, owner and remediation SLA
actions: Create one GRC finding per issue carrying the test record id, CI, test type, evidence reference and a plain description of the exposure.
Grade severity on the DORTP scale using exploitability plus the criticality of the function affected, not the raw CVSS score alone.
Apply the standard SLAs - critical 15 calendar days, high 30, medium 90, low 180 - measured from finding date, and let the platform compute the due date.
Assign a named remediation owner in the accountable IT team and notify them through the ITSM platform the same day.
Return to the tester any finding that names no CI or no owner rather than accepting it into the log.
checklist.done: every finding carries a severity, a CI, a named owner and an SLA-derived due date in the GRC platform.

checklist.step: Drive remediation to closure and re-test the fix
actions: Open a remediation task linked to each GRC finding and hold a weekly triage with the Vulnerability Management Lead / Security Engineering Lead on everything critical or high.
Require the fixing team to attach the change record number and post-change evidence to the task before requesting closure.
Ask the original tester to re-run the specific test that produced the finding and record pass or fail - closure without a re-test is not permitted.
Where the fix cannot land inside SLA, prepare a time-bound risk acceptance with compensating controls and route it to the Chief Info Security Officer.
Move the GRC finding to Closed-Verified only once the re-test result is attached.
checklist.done: no finding reaches Closed-Verified without an attached re-test result, and every SLA breach carries an approved time-bound risk acceptance.

checklist.step: Prove the annual coverage rule holds for every CIF system
actions: Each quarter export the completed test records from the GRC platform and left-join them onto the CIF register so systems with no completed test appear as blanks.
For each blank compute days since the last completed test of the required type and flag anything above 300 days as at risk of breaching the 12-month rule.
Chase each at-risk system with its system owner, re-date the test record, and escalate to the Head of IT where no date can be agreed.
Publish coverage percentage by tier on the quarterly resilience dashboard in Power BI.
checklist.done: the quarterly coverage report shows every CIF system inside 12 months of its required test, or names the owner and recovery date for each that is not.

checklist.step: Feed test outcomes back into the ICT risk management framework
actions: Map each material finding onto the ICT risk register entry it affects and re-score inherent and residual risk with the risk owner.
Where a scenario test broke an assumption in the business impact analysis, revise the RTO/RPO with the Business Continuity Manager and re-baseline it.
Update the Art. 6(5) ICT risk management framework document with the changes the year's testing forced and record the review date and approver.
Hand the revised risk positions to the Chief Risk Officer for the quarterly risk report.
checklist.done: every material finding is reflected in a re-scored risk register entry and the framework document records the resulting change.

checklist.step: Report the annual programme outcome to the management body
actions: Build the annual DORTP report - tests planned versus completed by tier, coverage percentage, findings raised by severity, open findings past SLA, outstanding risk acceptances and next year's plan.
State explicitly whether every CIF-supporting system met the at-least-annual testing requirement, naming any that did not and why.
Upload the pack to the board portal at least 5 business days before the Q4 meeting and present it with the Operational Resilience Lead.
Capture the management body's decisions - programme approval, additional investment, accepted risks - in the minutes and reflect them in next year's calendar.
checklist.done: the management body has approved the programme and its decisions on coverage gaps and risk acceptances are minuted.

checklist.step: Retain the evidence pack for supervisory request
actions: Assemble the annual pack - CIF register version, test-type matrix, test calendar with completion dates, test plans, results, finding log with ageing, risk acceptances, board pack and minutes.
File it under DORA/Art-24/<year> and apply the 5-year retention label.
Confirm the index makes the pack retrievable by CI id, CIF name, test type and completion date.
Record the pack location on the DORA obligation record so a supervisory response can be assembled inside the 10 business day service level.
checklist.done: the annual testing evidence pack is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by CI, function and test type.

testing.step: Build the population of CIF systems and executed tests for the year
actions: Export the CIF register as at 31 December with CI id, tier, system owner and supporting provider.
Export every DORTP test record with status Completed and a completion date inside the calendar year, with test type and tester name.
Independently pull the CMDB business-service mapping and compare CI counts to the CIF register, taking every difference to the Operational Resilience Lead before proceeding.
Sign the reconciled population as complete and record the extract timestamps in the workpaper.
testing.done: the CIF population reconciles to the CMDB business-service mapping and is signed as complete with dated extracts.

testing.step: Reconcile every CIF system to a completed test inside 12 months
actions: Left-join completed test records onto the CIF register on CI id and required test type.
Compute days between each completion date and the prior completion date and flag every gap above 365 days.
List systems with no completed test at all as automatic exceptions, with no allowance for tests still in flight at year end.
Check each flagged gap against the GRC audit trail so a back-dated completion date is visible.
testing.done: every CIF system is matched to a completed in-year test or listed as an exception with its gap in days.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample of tests
actions: Take 100 percent of Tier 1 CIF systems and 100 percent of tests covering an ICT third-party provider inside a CIF chain.
Take 25 further test records at random from the remaining population using a recorded seed, for a minimum of 40 records overall.
Record the population size, the seed, the selection date and the extract used so the sample can be redrawn identically.
Test in full any stratum holding fewer than 5 items instead of sampling it.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from a recorded seed and covers every Tier 1 system and third-party CIF test.

testing.step: Re-perform the test-type adequacy judgement against Art. 25(1)
actions: For each sampled system read the DORTP test-type matrix version in force at the test date and derive independently which test types were required for that tier.
Compare that to the test types actually executed and log any missing type as an exception, including where a lighter test type was substituted.
Read Art. 25(1) directly for the three highest-criticality sampled systems and confirm the matrix itself omits no listed test type.
Attach the matrix version and the Art. 25(1) text extract to the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled system has an independent adequacy conclusion and any substituted or missing test type is logged.

testing.step: Verify tester independence on the sample from entitlement data
actions: Take the named tester on each sampled test record and look up their entitlements to the tested CI as at the test date.
Treat any tester holding developer, administrator or change-approver rights on the system under test as an Art. 24(5) independence failure regardless of the attestation on file.
For external testers open the contract in the CLM repository and confirm the engagement was live on the test date and covered the tested scope.
Capture the entitlement screen and the contract reference into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled tester is evidenced as independent from entitlement data, or the independence failure is logged.

testing.step: Recompute vulnerability scan coverage from the tool
actions: Open the asset group used for the sampled scan and export the assets actually reached with the scan completion timestamp.
Compare that list to the CMDB CIF CI list as at the scan date and compute the real coverage percentage rather than relying on the reported figure.
For 5 CIs present in the CMDB but absent from the scan, establish with the Infrastructure / Network Engineer whether credentials, segmentation or a missing agent caused it.
Record the recomputed coverage and any difference from the coverage stated on the test record.
testing.done: scan coverage is recomputed from tool data and every difference from the reported figure is explained.

testing.step: Trace sampled tests to plans, results and evidence artefacts
actions: For each sampled test open the GRC record and confirm an approved test plan exists and is dated before the execution date.
Open the attached result artefact and confirm it names the same CIs, environment and test type as the plan.
Confirm the stated pass criteria were actually evaluated in the result and that no pass was recorded where a criterion went untested.
Where production-equivalence of a test environment was claimed, trace to the environment build record or the approved change.
Capture each artefact reference into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled test traces from a pre-dated plan to a matching result artefact evaluating its stated pass criteria.

testing.step: Recompute finding severities, SLA due dates and ageing
actions: Take all findings raised by the sampled tests and recompute the due date as finding date plus the DORTP SLA days for the recorded severity.
Compare to the due date held in the GRC platform and log every mismatch, particularly due dates edited after the fact.
For critical and high findings closed in the year, confirm a re-test result is attached and dated after the remediation change.
For findings open past SLA confirm a risk acceptance exists, is time-bound and is signed by the Chief Info Security Officer.
testing.done: SLA maths is recomputed for every sampled finding and each overdue item is matched to a signed, time-bound risk acceptance.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one GRC issue per exception naming the CIF system, the Art. 24 requirement missed and the supervisory consequence.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list - CIF register stale, calendar not maintained, tester not independent, test type substituted, remediation not re-tested, third party would not participate.
Name an accountable owner at Head of IT level or above and agree a remediation date inside the next quarter.
Carry every open exception into the following year's assurance test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a coded root cause, an owner, a dated remediation and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute coverage percentage by tier, the count of independence failures and the count of critical findings open past SLA at year end.
State a conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - against the zero-untested-CIF threshold, referencing the evidence behind it.
Have the reviewer, who scoped, executed and remediated none of the sampled tests, sign the workpaper with name and date.
Present the conclusion to the audit committee and the management body and file the signed workpaper under DORA/Art-24 in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper carries a stated conclusion, the coverage and exception statistics, and a recorded committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual management-body approval cycle for the DORA Art. 28(2) policy on the use of ICT services supporting critical or important functions; drafting sits with the Third-Party Risk Manager, tabling and minuting with the Corporate Secretary

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Art. 28(2) plus Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1773 (RTS on the policy for ICT services supporting critical or important functions performed by ICT third-party providers, including subcontracting) checked on EUR-Lex before each annual board tabling; EU authorised entities in scope

In-scope processes.value: Annual policy refresh cycle for the ICT third-party policy - horizon scan of DORA/RTS changes, gap assessment against Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1773 Arts. 1-10, redraft, second-line and legal challenge, management body approval, cascade to procurement/contracting/exit planning, and attestation that the full lifecycle (pre-contract due diligence, contracting, monitoring, subcontracting consent, exit) is covered

In-scope systems.value: Board portal holds the tabled policy, the approval resolution and the minutes; the GRC platform holds the policy record, its review date and the control mapping; the CLM repository holds the contract clause library the policy drives

Compliance procedure documented.value: Policy Governance Procedure for the ICT Third-Party Policy - review triggers, the Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1773 clause-by-clause gap template, the reviewer panel (CISO, Chief Risk Officer, General Counsel, Head of Compliance), the board paper format and the post-approval cascade checklist

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the management body itself as part of the annual policy suite approval; the procedure that governs the refresh is approved by the Chief Risk Officer and re-confirmed whenever an ESA guideline or RTS amendment lands

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: At least yearly review and management body approval under Art. 28(2), targeted at the Q4 board meeting so the approved policy is effective from 1 January; out-of-cycle review triggered within 60 days of a major ICT-related incident at a provider, a designation of a provider as critical, or an amendment to Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1773

Deadline reminders configured.value: GRC platform policy record raises reminders at T-120 days (start redraft), T-60 days (reviewer panel), T-20 days (board paper deadline) against the Q4 board date; the Corporate Secretary's board calendar carries the agenda item as a standing annual entry

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Each approved policy version, its redline against the prior version, the gap assessment, reviewer comments, the board paper, the approval resolution and the minute extract retained 10 years in the board records archive and 5 years in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A missed annual approval, a policy operating past its review date, and any contract or arrangement entered outside the approved policy are each raised as a governance issue with the responsible executive named and a board-reported remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The Corporate Secretary confirms in the minutes that the management body approved the version presented and signs the certified true copy that goes into the evidence pack

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The ICT third-party policy record and every approval event in the last 24 months, plus all ICT arrangements supporting a critical or important function entered or renewed since the last approved version took effect

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Approved policy version with effective date, certified minute extract recording the approval, the Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1773 coverage matrix and the version history, deliverable to the competent authority within 5 business days of request

checklist.step: Open the annual review 120 days before the Q4 board date
actions: In the GRC platform open Policies ▸ ICT Third-Party Policy and confirm the recorded last-approval date and next-review date.
Compute the drop-dead approval date as last approval plus 12 months and take the earlier of that and the Q4 board date as the target.
Ask the Corporate Secretary to confirm the Q4 board date and the paper submission deadline, and book the agenda item.
Open a review workspace and name the drafter (Third-Party Risk Manager), the reviewer panel and the approving body on the record.
checklist.done: the review is open with a target board date inside 12 months of the last approval and a named drafter, panel and approver.

checklist.step: Horizon-scan for DORA and RTS changes since the last approval
actions: Pull the EUR-Lex change history for Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 and Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1773 since the last approval date.
Review ESA (EBA/EIOPA/ESMA) publications, Q&As and the register of designated critical ICT third-party providers for anything that changes the policy's obligations.
Take the national competent authority's DORA circulars and supervisory expectations from the Government Affairs Manager and list any local add-on.
Write a one-page change log stating, for each item, whether the policy must change and which clause is affected.
checklist.done: a dated change log lists every regulatory development since the last approval with a policy-impact call on each.

checklist.step: Run the clause-by-clause gap assessment against Art. 28(2) and the RTS
actions: Build a matrix with one row per requirement drawn from Art. 28(2) and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1773 - governance and roles, pre-contractual due diligence and risk assessment, criticality determination, conflicts of interest, contractual content, subcontracting conditions and consent, monitoring of performance and risk, exit strategies and transition plans, register maintenance.
Against each row cite the current policy section number and paste the operative sentence, or write GAP.
Confirm the policy covers the full lifecycle end to end - Art. 28(2) requires it, and a policy that stops at contract signature is a gap.
Send the matrix with GAP rows highlighted to the drafter and the General Counsel with a two-week response window.
checklist.done: every Art. 28(2) and RTS requirement maps to a cited policy section or is recorded as an explicit gap with an owner.

checklist.step: Redraft the policy to close the gaps
actions: Draft in tracked changes on the approved version so the board sees exactly what moved.
For each gap row write the operative requirement in obligation language - who must do what, by when, with what approval - rather than descriptive prose.

Set out the subcontracting conditions the RTS requires, including which subcontracting of CIF-supporting services needs prior written consent and what the entity may do when a provider subcontracts without it.
State the escalation and termination triggers, including failure to meet agreed service levels and inability to exercise audit and access rights.
Version the draft as v<n>-draft with the change log attached and store it in the policy SharePoint library.
checklist.done: a tracked-change draft closes every GAP row with operative, testable obligations and a versioned change log.

checklist.step: Put the draft through the second-line and legal reviewer panel
actions: Circulate the draft to the Chief Info Security Officer, the Chief Risk Officer, the Head of Compliance and the Procurement Manager with the gap matrix.
Hold a single challenge session, minute the objections and record for each one whether the draft changed and who decided.
Confirm the drafted subcontracting and audit-rights language is enforceable in every jurisdiction the entity contracts from, taking local counsel input where it is not.
Close the review only when every reviewer has recorded agreement or a documented dissent.
checklist.done: each panel reviewer has a recorded agreement or dissent and every objection has a documented disposition.

checklist.step: Align the policy with the contract clause library before tabling
actions: Open the ICT services clause set in the CLM repository and map each mandatory Art. 30(2) and Art. 30(3) contractual element to the standard clause that delivers it.
Where the redrafted policy adds a requirement with no clause behind it, draft the clause now so the policy is operable on its effective date.
Flag every in-force CIF contract that would breach the new policy and list them for the transition plan.
Record the clause-library version number in the policy so future changes stay paired.
checklist.done: every new policy requirement has a matching standard clause and non-conforming in-force CIF contracts are listed.

checklist.step: Write the board paper with a decision, not a description
actions: Write the paper to the board template - purpose, the specific approval sought, what changed and why, residual risks, the population of CIF arrangements affected, and the implementation plan with dates.
State the legal basis on the front page: annual management body approval required by Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Art. 28(2).
Attach the clean policy, the redline, the gap matrix and the list of non-conforming in-force contracts.
Have the Chief Risk Officer and the General Counsel sign the paper as sponsors before submission.
checklist.done: the paper states the approval sought and the Art. 28(2) basis, and carries sponsor signatures and the four attachments.

checklist.step: Table the paper to the management body inside the deadline
actions: Upload the paper and attachments to the board portal at least 5 business days before the meeting and confirm every director's access.
Place it on the agenda as a decision item, not for noting, and record the agenda reference.
Check no director has an interest requiring recusal - for instance a directorship at a contracted ICT provider - and record the conflicts check.
Track the portal read receipts and chase any director who has not opened the paper 48 hours out.
checklist.done: the paper is on the agenda as a decision item, distributed 5 business days ahead, with a completed conflicts check.

checklist.step: Secure and minute the management body approval
actions: Record the resolution wording naming the policy title, the version number and the effective date approved.
Minute the substantive challenge the board gave - Art. 28(2) expects the management body to actually govern this, and silent approval reads badly at supervision.
Capture any conditions the board attached and convert each into an action with an owner and a due date.
Issue the certified minute extract and file it with the approved policy version.
checklist.done: the minutes name the approved version and effective date, record the board's challenge, and every condition is an owned action.

checklist.step: Publish the approved version and retire the superseded one
actions: Load the approved PDF into the GRC policy record with version number, approval date, effective date and next-review date set to approval plus 12 months.
Mark the prior version Superseded rather than deleting it, so the version in force on any past date can be established.
Publish to the policy portal and push a read-and-acknowledge task to Procurement, Vendor Management, IT and Legal staff who contract for ICT services.
Track acknowledgement completion and chase anyone outstanding after 30 days.
checklist.done: the approved version is live with a next-review date set, the prior version is marked superseded, and acknowledgements are tracked.

checklist.step: Cascade the policy into procurement and contracting controls
actions: Update the sourcing intake form so any request touching an ICT service triggers the CIF criticality question and routes to the Third-Party Risk Manager.
Configure the approval workflow so a CIF-supporting ICT contract cannot progress to award without a completed pre-contractual risk assessment and the required clause set.
Brief the category managers on what changed, using the redline, and record attendance.
Test the workflow with one dummy requisition and confirm the block actually fires.
checklist.done: the procurement workflow blocks a CIF ICT award without the policy-required assessment, proven by a test requisition.

checklist.step: Bring non-conforming in-force arrangements onto a transition plan
actions: Take the list of in-force CIF contracts that fail the new policy and open each in the CLM repository.
For each, name the failing requirement, the amendment or waiver needed and the next renewal or break date.
Agree a remediation date with the contract owner, preferring the next renewal window where the gap is not a DORA mandatory clause and immediate amendment where it is.
Report the plan and its ageing to the Chief Risk Officer monthly until the list is clear.
checklist.done: every non-conforming in-force CIF contract has a named gap, a remediation route and a dated plan under monthly reporting.

checklist.step: Arm the out-of-cycle review triggers
actions: Configure GRC rules so a major ICT-related incident at a CIF provider, a new ESA designation of a critical ICT third-party provider, or an amendment to Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1773 raises a policy-review task automatically.
Set the task SLA to 60 days from trigger to a decision on whether the policy must change.
Route the task to the Third-Party Risk Manager with the Board Governance Lead as watcher.
Record the trigger, the decision and the rationale on the policy record even where no change is made.
checklist.done: the three out-of-cycle triggers raise an automatic 60-day review task and every trigger is dispositioned on the record.

checklist.step: Confirm the policy is reflected in the ICT risk framework and the Register of Information
actions: Check the Art. 6 ICT risk management framework document references the approved policy version and effective date.
Confirm the Register of Information fields the policy relies on - criticality flag, subcontracting chain, exit plan reference - exist and are populated for CIF arrangements.
Where the policy created a new data requirement, raise a change request with the Third-Party Risk Manager to add it to the register template.
Report alignment status into the quarterly ICT risk report to the risk committee.
checklist.done: the framework document cites the approved version and every policy-driven register field exists and is populated for CIF arrangements.

checklist.step: File the approval evidence pack for supervisory production
actions: Assemble the pack - approved policy PDF, redline, gap matrix, board paper, certified minute extract, publication record and acknowledgement report.
File under DORA/Art-28-2/<year> with the 10-year board-records retention label and index it by version number and approval date.
Record the pack location on the DORA obligation record so it can be produced within the 5 business day supervisory service level.
Confirm read access for the Head of Compliance and the Chief Audit Executive and restrict edit access.
checklist.done: the approval evidence pack is filed, retention-labelled, indexed by version and retrievable within the 5 business day service level.

testing.step: Build the population of policy versions and approval events
actions: Export the full version history of the ICT third-party policy record with version number, status, approval date, effective date and next-review date.
Export the board portal agenda and minute index for the last 24 months and pull every item referencing the policy.
Reconcile the two - a version marked approved in the GRC platform with no matching board item, or a board approval with no GRC version, is investigated before testing continues.
Sign the reconciled population and record the extract dates.
testing.done: GRC version history and board minutes reconcile item for item over 24 months and the population is signed as complete.

testing.step: Recompute the approval interval against the 12-month rule
actions: Sort approval events by date and compute the elapsed days between consecutive management body approvals.
Flag any interval above 365 days as a fail against the at-least-yearly requirement in Art. 28(2).
Check the effective date of each approved version against the approval date so no version was in force before it was approved.
Identify any period where no approved, in-date version existed and list the CIF contracts signed in that window.
testing.done: approval intervals are recomputed, every interval above 365 days is a logged fail and contracts signed in any lapse window are listed.

testing.step: Re-perform the Art. 28(2) and RTS coverage assessment independently
actions: Read Art. 28(2) and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1773 from EUR-Lex and build an independent requirement list without looking at management's gap matrix.
Map each requirement to the approved policy text and record the section number, marking anything unaddressed as a coverage exception.
Pay particular attention to full-lifecycle coverage and to the subcontracting conditions and consent rules, which are the most commonly thin sections.
Compare the independent list to management's matrix and report any requirement management omitted from its own assessment.
testing.done: an independent requirement list is mapped to the approved policy and every unaddressed requirement is logged as a coverage exception.

testing.step: Trace the approval to primary board records
actions: Open the board portal meeting record for the approval and read the resolution wording as minuted.
Confirm the minute names the policy title, version number and effective date rather than approving 'the policy' generically.
Check the attendance and quorum record and confirm the conflicts check was performed and any interested director recused.
Confirm the paper was distributed at least 5 business days ahead by reading the portal publication timestamp, not the paper's own date.
Capture the minute extract and the distribution timestamp into the workpaper.
testing.done: the minuted resolution names the exact version approved and the portal timestamp evidences distribution inside the notice period.

testing.step: Test that the version in force governed the contracts actually signed
actions: Draw all ICT arrangements supporting a CIF that were signed or renewed in the period from the CLM repository.
For each, determine which policy version was effective on the signature date from the GRC version history.

Sample 20 contracts, or the whole set if fewer, and check the required clause set for that version is present - audit and access rights, subcontracting consent, service levels, exit assistance, data location.
Record the seed and selection date so the sample can be redrawn.
testing.done: each sampled contract is tested against the policy version effective on its signature date, with the sample reproducible from a recorded seed.

testing.step: Verify the out-of-cycle triggers actually fired
actions: List the major ICT-related incidents at CIF providers, ESA critical-provider designations and RTS amendments that occurred in the period, sourced independently of the policy record.
For each, check whether a GRC review task was raised and whether it was dispositioned inside the 60-day SLA.
Read the recorded rationale where no policy change was made and assess whether it engages with the trigger substantively.
Log any trigger with no task or no disposition as an exception.
testing.done: every independently identified trigger event maps to a raised, dispositioned review task or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Test the procurement cascade with a walkthrough
actions: Raise a test requisition for an ICT service flagged as CIF-supporting and attempt to advance it to award without the pre-contractual risk assessment.
Confirm the workflow blocks the award and names the missing artefact rather than issuing a soft warning.
Repeat with the assessment attached and confirm the required clause set is applied automatically to the resulting contract record.
Screenshot both outcomes into the workpaper and record the test requisition numbers.
testing.done: the workflow is proven to hard-block a CIF ICT award without the policy-required assessment, with both walkthrough screens captured.

testing.step: Check acknowledgement coverage across the accountable population
actions: Take the intended audience list - Procurement, Vendor Management, IT contracting and Legal staff - from the HRIS org structure rather than from the policy tool's own distribution list.
Compare it to the acknowledgement report and compute the completion percentage and the count of never-acknowledged staff.
Investigate any group missing from the distribution list entirely, which indicates a cascade design gap rather than an individual lapse.
Record the recomputed coverage against the 100 percent expectation.
testing.done: acknowledgement coverage is recomputed against an independently derived audience and every excluded group is investigated.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the Art. 28(2) or RTS element missed and the governance consequence.
Assign a root cause from the list - review not scheduled, board date slipped, gap assessment incomplete, minute wording generic, cascade not configured, trigger not armed.
Name an executive owner and a remediation date, and require any lapsed-approval finding to be reported to the audit committee at its next sitting.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a coded root cause, an executive owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Summarise the maximum approval interval observed, the count of unaddressed RTS requirements and the count of contracts signed during any lapse window.
State a conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - against the zero-lapse and full-coverage thresholds.
Have the reviewer, who neither drafted, reviewed nor tabled the policy, sign the workpaper with name and date.
Report to the audit committee and the management body and file the signed workpaper under DORA/Art-28-2 in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper carries the interval and coverage statistics, a stated conclusion and a recorded committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the DORA Art. 28(3) Register of Information at entity, sub-consolidated and consolidated level and its annual submission to the national competent authority; the Chief Info Security Officer countersigns the submission and the Chief Risk Officer owns the escalation of unresolved data gaps

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Art. 28(3) and Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2956 (ITS on the templates for the Register of Information) checked on EUR-Lex, alongside the ESAs' current reporting instructions and data point model, before each annual build; obligation applicable from 17 January 2025 with the first collection run in 2025

In-scope processes.value: Contract intake and CLM data capture -> ICT service classification and criticality assessment -> LEI and EUID sourcing for every provider and in-scope entity -> supply-chain (subcontracting) mapping for CIF services -> build of the ITS templates B_01.01 to B_07.01 at entity, sub-consolidated and consolidated level -> validation, sign-off and machine-readable submission

In-scope systems.value: The CLM repository is the source of record for contractual arrangements and their terms; the GRC platform holds criticality assessments and function mapping; Enterprise Reference Data (MDM/RDM) holds LEI, EUID and legal-entity hierarchy; the register file is assembled and validated before submission through the competent authority's reporting channel

Compliance procedure documented.value: Register of Information Procedure - template-by-template data dictionary against ITS (EU) 2024/2956, the ownership matrix per data field, the LEI/EUID sourcing rules, the reference-date freeze process, the validation rule set and the sign-off and submission runbook

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Info Security Officer and the Chief Risk Officer; re-approved each time the ESAs reissue the reporting instructions, the data point model or the validation rules

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Register maintained continuously and updated within 10 business days of any new, amended or terminated ICT arrangement; reported at least yearly to the competent authority against the 31 March reference date, submitted in the window the national competent authority publishes each year (typically April); ad-hoc submission whenever the competent authority requests it

Deadline reminders configured.value: GRC calendar drives the annual cycle - T-90 days source data freeze notice to contract owners, T-60 days LEI and EUID completeness check, T-30 days validation run, T-10 days sign-off, plus the national submission deadline itself; CLM raises a 10-business-day task on every contract create, amend or terminate event

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Each submitted register file, the validation report, the reconciliation to the CLM contract population, the criticality assessment evidence and the signed submission approval retained 5 years from the reference date in the compliance evidence repository, alongside the submission acknowledgement from the competent authority

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Missing or invalid LEI, an unmapped CIF-supporting arrangement, a subcontracting chain not traced to the rank supporting a CIF, a failed validation rule accepted into the submission, and a late submission are each logged as a data-quality or reporting issue with an owner and a correction date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The CISO signs the register as complete and accurate before submission and approves any residual data gap that goes out with the file, naming the correction date

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every contractual arrangement for ICT services in force at the 31 March reference date across all in-scope legal entities, plus every arrangement created, amended or terminated during the year, matched to the rows in the submitted register templates

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Fail if any in-force ICT arrangement at the reference date is absent from the register, if any CIF-supporting arrangement lacks a criticality assessment or a subcontracting chain to the required rank, if any provider row carries a missing or non-conforming LEI, if a validation rule was overridden without CISO approval, or if the submission missed the competent authority's deadline; any absent CIF arrangement is a fail regardless of materiality

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is continuous maintenance with an annual report at the 31 March reference date, so assurance runs annually on the submitted file plus a quarterly maintenance check that contract events reached the register inside 10 business days

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: The auditor must not have populated, validated or signed the register and must be able to pull the CLM and MDM extracts directly rather than receiving them from the preparer

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual Register of Information assurance workpaper - CLM population extract, template-by-template reconciliation, LEI validation output, criticality re-performance, subcontracting trace and exception log - in the compliance evidence repository under DORA/Art-28-3/<reference year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The submitted machine-readable register file, the validation report, the submission acknowledgement, the reconciliation to the contract population and the CISO sign-off, producible to the competent authority or the Lead Overseer within 5 business days of request

Regulator response path.value: The Third-Party Risk Manager answers data queries from the competent authority, the Regulatory Reporting Manager controls resubmissions and version numbering, and the Chief Info Security Officer signs any corrected file; the Head of Compliance is copied on every exchange

checklist.step: Freeze the contract population at the reference date
actions: Notify all contract owners 90 days out that the register reference date is 31 March and that CLM records must be current by then.

On the reference date export every contractual arrangement for ICT services with contract reference, contracting entity, provider, service description, start date, end or renewal date, notice period, governing law and annual expense.
Include intra-group ICT arrangements - Art. 28(3) does not exempt them - and flag them so template B_02.03 can be built.
Take a second extract from the accounts payable ledger of vendors with ICT spend and chase any vendor with spend but no CLM contract record.
Lock the extract as the reference-date population and record its timestamp and row count.
checklist.done: a locked, timestamped reference-date contract population exists and reconciles to ICT vendor spend in the ledger.

checklist.step: Classify each arrangement as an ICT service and assign the ITS service type
actions: Test each contract against the DORA Art. 3(21) definition of ICT services and drop non-ICT arrangements with a written reason on the row.
Assign the ITS ICT service type code from the reporting instructions to every retained row, using the service actually consumed rather than the vendor's marketing description.
Where one contract covers several service types, split it into the separate rows the templates require and keep the contract reference on each.
Have the service owner confirm the type code in writing for every CIF-supporting arrangement.
checklist.done: each retained arrangement carries an ITS service type code, with multi-service contracts split and CIF codes owner-confirmed.

checklist.step: Run the criticality assessment behind template B_07.01
actions: For each ICT service map the business function it supports and pull that function's critical-or-important determination from the CIF register.

Record the assessment inputs the ITS asks for - whether the service supports a critical or important function, the substitutability of the provider, the possibility of reintegration, the impact of discontinuation and the existence of an exit plan.
Have the function owner and the Chief Info Security Officer sign the determination for every service judged CIF-supporting.
Attach the assessment record id to the register row so the file can be defended line by line.
checklist.done: every ICT service has a signed criticality determination with its ITS assessment fields populated and linked to the register row.

checklist.step: Source and validate LEI and EUID identifiers for every party
actions: For each ICT third-party provider retrieve the ISO 17442 LEI from GLEIF and store it in MDM against the vendor master record.
Check each LEI's registration status is Issued and its next renewal date has not lapsed - a lapsed LEI fails the ITS validation.
For each in-scope EU legal entity record the LEI and, where required by the template, the EUID from the national business register.
Where a provider has no LEI, escalate to the Vendor Manager to obtain one and log the gap with a target date rather than leaving the field blank.
Publish the identifier completeness report to the Third-Party Risk Manager 60 days before submission.
checklist.done: every provider and in-scope entity row carries a valid, non-lapsed identifier, or a logged gap with an owner and a target date.

checklist.step: Map the ICT subcontracting chains for CIF-supporting services
actions: For every CIF-supporting service ask the direct provider in writing for its subcontractors that effectively underpin that service, with each subcontractor's legal name, country and LEI.
Record the chain by rank - rank 1 the direct provider, rank 2 its subcontractor, and onward to the rank at which the CIF-supporting service is actually delivered - so template B_05.02 can be built.
Where a provider refuses to disclose its chain, raise the contractual right under the ICT third-party policy with the Contracts Manager and log the disclosure gap.
Reconcile the disclosed chains to what the Vendor Manager sees in the annual assurance reports and challenge any difference.
checklist.done: each CIF-supporting service has a ranked subcontracting chain with identifiers, or a logged disclosure gap with a contractual escalation.

checklist.step: Build the register templates at every required reporting level
actions: Populate the ITS templates in order - B_01.01 to B_01.03 for the reporting entity, branches and entities in scope; B_02.01 to B_02.03 for the contractual arrangements including intra-group; B_03.01 to B_03.03 for the signing parties; B_04.01 for the entities making use of the services; B_05.01 and B_05.02 for providers and supply chains; B_06.01 for functions; B_07.01 for the CIF service assessment.
Build the file at entity level first, then sub-consolidated, then consolidated, keeping the entity-level files as the audit trail behind the consolidated one.
Apply the ITS enumerations exactly - country codes, currency codes, service type codes and function identifiers - rather than free text.
Reconcile row counts between related templates so every contract row has a signing party, a using entity and a function.
Save each level as a separate versioned file named <entity>-RoI-<reference date>-v<n>.
checklist.done: templates B_01.01 to B_07.01 are populated at entity, sub-consolidated and consolidated level with cross-template row counts reconciling.

checklist.step: Run the ESA validation rules and clear every failure
actions: Run the current ESA validation rule set and the data point model checks against the file before any submission attempt.
Work every blocking failure to zero - referential breaks between templates, invalid LEIs, missing mandatory fields, enumeration values outside the code list.
For non-blocking warnings, record on each one whether the data is right and the warning is expected, or the data is wrong and is being corrected.
Re-run the full rule set after every correction rather than spot-fixing, and keep the final clean validation report as evidence.
checklist.done: the final validation run shows zero blocking failures and every warning carries a written disposition.

checklist.step: Reconcile the register back to the contract and spend populations
actions: Match register contract rows to the locked CLM reference-date population on contract reference and list both unmatched directions.
Reconcile the provider list to ICT vendor spend in the ERP general ledger and investigate any vendor with material ICT spend absent from the register.
Confirm every arrangement flagged CIF-supporting in the GRC platform appears in template B_07.01.
Document each reconciling item with a reason and a correction, and get the Third-Party Risk Manager to accept the residual difference in writing.
checklist.done: the register reconciles to the CLM population and to ICT vendor spend, with every reconciling item explained and accepted in writing.

checklist.step: Obtain the sign-off before submission
actions: Review the submission pack - the file at each level, the validation report, the reconciliation and the open data-gap list with owners and dates.
Challenge any CIF-supporting arrangement carrying an incomplete subcontracting chain or a missing exit plan reference before signing.
Sign the completeness and accuracy statement naming the reference date, the file version and the reporting levels covered.
Where a residual gap goes out with the file, record the gap, its cause and its correction date in the sign-off so it can be disclosed if the authority asks.
checklist.done: a signed completeness and accuracy statement names the reference date, file version and every residual gap with its correction date.

checklist.step: Submit the register to the competent authority in the prescribed format
actions: Convert the approved file into the machine-readable format the ITS and the national competent authority require and confirm the file naming and reporting-period conventions from its current instructions.
Submit through the competent authority's reporting channel inside the window it published for the 31 March reference date and capture the submission reference and timestamp.
Save the technical acknowledgement or receipt as the proof of filing and check it reports no rejection.
Where the authority rejects the file, correct, re-validate and resubmit inside the deadline, keeping every version rather than overwriting.
Notify the Chief Info Security Officer and the Head of Compliance that the submission is confirmed.
checklist.done: the submission is accepted inside the published window with a stored acknowledgement reference and every rejected version retained.

checklist.step: Keep the register current through the year on a 10-business-day clock
actions: Configure the CLM repository so contract create, amend, renew and terminate events raise a register-update task within one business day.
Require the contract owner to complete the register fields - service type, function supported, criticality, provider identifier, subcontracting chain where CIF - within 10 business days of the event.
Run a weekly ageing report of open register-update tasks and escalate anything past 10 business days to the Third-Party Risk Manager.
Reflect terminations promptly so the register does not carry arrangements that have ended.
checklist.done: every contract event raises a register-update task and the weekly ageing report shows no task open beyond 10 business days.

checklist.step: Run the quarterly completeness sweep between annual submissions
actions: Each quarter compare the live register to the CLM contract population and to ICT vendor spend and publish the three counts side by side.
Re-validate all provider LEIs against GLEIF and flag any that lapsed since the last check.
Report the CIF-supporting arrangements missing a subcontracting chain or an exit plan reference by provider and by owner.
Publish the dashboard to the Third-Party Risk Manager and the Chief Info Security Officer with the movement since last quarter.
checklist.done: the quarterly dashboard shows register-to-CLM-to-spend counts, lapsed LEIs and CIF data gaps by owner, with quarter-on-quarter movement.

checklist.step: Respond to competent authority and Lead Overseer follow-up queries
actions: Log every query from the competent authority with its date, the templates and rows it touches, and the response deadline.
Trace each queried row back to the CLM contract and the criticality assessment before answering, so the response is sourced rather than asserted.
Where the query reveals an error, correct the underlying record first and resubmit the register with a new version number.
Have the Head of Compliance clear every written response and file the exchange with the submission pack.
checklist.done: every authority query has a dated log entry, a source-traced response cleared by Compliance, and a resubmission where an error was found.

checklist.step: Report register health to the management body
actions: Present the annual submission outcome - date submitted, acknowledgement reference, count of arrangements, count of CIF-supporting arrangements and residual data gaps.
Show the concentration picture the register reveals - providers supporting more than one CIF, and functions dependent on a single provider or a single subcontracting chain.
Ask the management body to decide on any concentration the register exposes, and minute the decision.
Feed the concentration findings to the Third-Party Risk Manager for the next exit-planning cycle.
checklist.done: the management body has seen the submission outcome and the concentration picture and its decisions are minuted.

checklist.step: File the submission evidence pack
actions: Assemble the pack - locked reference-date population, each level's register file, validation reports, reconciliations, criticality assessments, CISO sign-off, submitted file and acknowledgement.
File under DORA/Art-28-3/<reference year> with a 5-year retention label from the reference date.
Index by reference date, reporting level, provider LEI and contract reference so a single arrangement can be traced across years.
Record the pack location on the DORA obligation record for the 5 business day supervisory production service level.
checklist.done: the submission evidence pack is filed, retention-labelled and indexed so any single arrangement is traceable across reference years.

testing.step: Rebuild the in-force contract population independently
actions: Pull the auditor's own extract of ICT contractual arrangements in force at 31 March directly from the CLM repository rather than accepting the preparer's file.
Add ICT vendors from the ERP accounts payable ledger with spend in the 12 months to the reference date.
Compare the auditor extract to the preparer's locked population and investigate every difference in both directions.
Sign the reconciled test population and record both extract timestamps.
testing.done: an independently pulled population reconciles to the preparer's locked file, with every difference in both directions investigated.

testing.step: Reconcile the submitted register to the test population
actions: Match submitted register contract rows to the test population on contract reference and provider identifier.
List every in-force arrangement absent from the register and every register row with no supporting contract as automatic exceptions.
Compare counts template by template - contracts, providers, using entities, functions - against the expected relationships.
Confirm intra-group ICT arrangements appear rather than having been treated as out of scope.
testing.done: every in-force arrangement is matched to a register row or listed as an exception, and intra-group arrangements are confirmed present.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample across the register
actions: Take 100 percent of arrangements flagged as supporting a critical or important function.
Take 25 further arrangements at random from the remainder using a recorded seed, for at least 40 rows in total.
Stratify to include at least 5 intra-group arrangements and 5 arrangements added during the year.
Record population size, seed and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
testing.done: the sample covers all CIF arrangements plus a reproducible random selection with intra-group and in-year additions represented.

testing.step: Re-perform the criticality determination on the sample
actions: For each sampled arrangement read the service description and the supported business function and reach an independent critical-or-important conclusion before opening the recorded assessment.
Compare to the B_07.01 flag and record any difference, treating a CIF service recorded as non-CIF as a reportable exception.
Confirm the ITS assessment fields - substitutability, reintegration, impact of discontinuation, exit plan existence - are populated with substantive answers and not defaults.
Confirm the function owner and CISO sign-offs exist and pre-date the submission.
testing.done: each sampled arrangement has an independent criticality conclusion, and every difference from the recorded flag is logged.

testing.step: Re-validate provider identifiers against GLEIF
actions: Take the provider LEIs from the submitted file and look each up in GLEIF as at the reference date.
Check the legal name on the LEI record matches the provider name in the register and that the registration status was Issued, not Lapsed, on the reference date.
Flag any provider row with a blank identifier, a checksum-invalid LEI, or an LEI belonging to a different legal entity in the group.
Record the recomputed identifier error rate against the zero-tolerance threshold.
testing.done: every sampled provider identifier is verified against GLEIF as at the reference date and the error rate is recomputed.

testing.step: Trace subcontracting chains to provider evidence
actions: For each sampled CIF arrangement open the provider's written subcontractor disclosure and compare it to the ranked chain in template B_05.02.
Confirm the chain runs to the rank at which the CIF-supporting service is actually delivered rather than stopping at rank 1.
Cross-check the disclosed subcontractors against the provider's assurance report scope and challenge any subcontractor named there but absent from the register.
Log an exception where a chain rests on assertion with no dated written disclosure behind it.
testing.done: every sampled CIF chain traces to a dated written provider disclosure and runs to the delivering rank.

testing.step: Re-run the ESA validation rules on the submitted file
actions: Run the current ESA validation rule set against the exact file that was submitted, not a working copy.
Confirm zero blocking failures and compare the warning list to the dispositions recorded before submission.
Check the enumerations used - country, currency, service type, function identifier - all sit inside the ITS code lists.
Log any override applied without a recorded CISO approval as an exception.
testing.done: re-running the rules on the submitted file reproduces zero blocking failures and every warning disposition is confirmed.

testing.step: Recompute submission timing and maintenance lags
actions: Compare the submission timestamp on the acknowledgement to the competent authority's published deadline for the 31 March reference date and compute the days of margin or lateness.
For arrangements created, amended or terminated during the year, compute the elapsed business days between the contract event date in CLM and the register update.
Flag every update beyond 10 business days and compute the mean and worst-case lag.
Confirm terminated arrangements were removed rather than left in force in the file.
testing.done: submission timing and every maintenance lag are recomputed, with all updates beyond 10 business days flagged.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and correction date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the template and field affected and the supervisory consequence under Art. 28(3).
Assign a root cause from the list - contract not in CLM, service not classified, criticality not assessed, LEI not sourced, chain not disclosed, validation overridden, submission late.
Name an owner and a correction date, and decide with the Regulatory Reporting Manager whether the exception requires a corrected resubmission rather than a next-cycle fix.
Carry every open exception into the next reference year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a coded root cause, an owner, a correction date and a documented resubmit-or-not decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Summarise arrangements absent from the register, identifier error rate, incomplete CIF chains, validation overrides and days of submission margin.
State a conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - against the zero-missing-CIF-arrangement and on-time-submission thresholds.
Have the reviewer, who neither populated, validated nor signed the register, sign the workpaper with name and date.
Report to the audit committee and file the signed workpaper under DORA/Art-28-3 in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper carries the completeness and timeliness statistics, a stated conclusion and a recorded committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the Art. 6(6)-(7) internal audit of the ICT risk management framework, the ICT competence of the auditors performing it and the formal follow-up process on critical ICT audit findings; reports the outcome directly to the audit committee and the management body

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Art. 6(6) and 6(7) read on EUR-Lex alongside Arts. 24-25 for the testing programme the audit covers, re-checked when the risk-based audit plan is approved each year; EU authorised entities in scope, with group internal audit standards (IIA) applied on top

In-scope processes.value: Annual ICT audit universe refresh -> risk-based ICT audit plan approved by the audit committee -> auditor ICT competence assessment -> execution of the ICT risk management framework audit (governance, identification, protection and prevention, detection, response and recovery, learning and evolving, communication, third-party risk, testing) -> finding grading -> formal follow-up and verification of remediation for critical findings

In-scope systems.value: AuditBoard holds the ICT audit universe, plan, fieldwork, findings and follow-up verification; the GRC platform supplies the ICT risk register and control library the audit tests against; ITSM holds the remediation tasks the audit tracks to closure

Compliance procedure documented.value: ICT Internal Audit Procedure - ICT audit universe definition, the risk-scoring model driving frequency, auditor ICT competence criteria and evidencing, the DORA Art. 5-16 test programme, finding severity definitions, and the formal follow-up standard requiring re-performance rather than management assertion for critical findings

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the audit committee on the Chief Audit Executive's recommendation; the annual risk-based ICT audit plan is separately approved by the audit committee before the year starts and any in-year change to it is re-approved there

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Risk-based ICT audit plan approved before 31 December for the following year; the ICT risk management framework audited at least once in the plan cycle with high-risk domains covered annually; critical findings verified closed within 90 days of the agreed remediation date; follow-up status reported to the audit committee every quarter

Deadline reminders configured.value: AuditBoard raises milestone alerts for plan approval (T-45 days to year end), fieldwork start and report issue dates per engagement, and finding due dates at T-30, T-7 and T+1 days; overdue critical ICT findings appear on the audit committee dashboard automatically

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Audit universe, approved plan, auditor competence records, engagement workpapers, issued reports, management responses, follow-up verification evidence and audit committee minutes retained 7 years from report issue in the audit workpaper archive and referenced from the compliance evidence repository
