actions: Upload the certification, the aggregate breakdown and the framework review outcome to the board portal for the meeting following certification.
Present the loss drivers and the concentration by critical or important function so the board sees where resilience investment is warranted.
Minute the management body's noting or approval and any direction it gives on remediation investment.
File the minute extract with the certification pack.
checklist.done: the management body has seen the certified figure and the loss drivers and its directions are minuted.

checklist.step: Hold the pack production-ready for an Art. 11(10) request
actions: Assemble the production pack - certification, aggregate and breakdown, per-incident schedule, method note, ledger and loss database reconciliations, framework review record.
Store it under DORA/Art-11-10/<financial year> with read access pre-granted to the Head of Compliance and the Chief Info Security Officer.
Write and rehearse the production runbook so the pack can be released inside 10 business days of a request, including who redacts what.
Re-check the pack each quarter so late-settling recoveries and provisions are reflected before a request arrives.
checklist.done: the production pack is assembled, access-controlled, quarterly refreshed and covered by a rehearsed 10 business day release runbook.

checklist.step: Respond to the competent authority's request when it comes
actions: Log the request with its date, the exact scope asked for and the response deadline the authority set.
Check whether the request covers a period already certified or requires an interim figure, and where interim, run the same method on a part-year basis and label it as such.
Have the Chief Financial Officer confirm the figures being sent still agree to the ledger position at the response date.
Submit through the authority's channel, store the acknowledgement and log any follow-up question with its answer.
checklist.done: the request, the scope, the submitted figures, the CFO confirmation and the acknowledgement are all on the log with follow-ups tracked.

checklist.step: Improve the cost capture during the year rather than after it
actions: Make the cost worksheet a mandatory closure artefact on every major incident so amounts are captured while the facts are fresh.
Add an incident reference field to purchase requisitions and expense claims so external costs are tagged at source rather than hunted afterwards.
Run a half-year completeness check on worksheet coverage and chase incident owners with gaps.
Report worksheet coverage monthly to the Chief Info Security Officer alongside the incident metrics.
checklist.done: cost worksheets are mandatory at incident closure, external spend is tagged at source, and coverage is reported monthly.

checklist.step: File the certification evidence and retire the prior year
actions: File the signed certification, locked workbook, worksheets, reconciliations, method note and board minute under DORA/Art-11-10/<financial year>.
Apply the 5-year retention label from the certification date and mark the prior year's pack as superseded but retained.
Index by financial year, incident reference and cost category so a single incident's cost can be traced across the register, the ledger and the estimate.
Record the pack location on the DORA obligation record for the 10 business day production service level.
checklist.done: the certification pack is filed, retention-labelled and indexed so any incident's cost is traceable across register, ledger and estimate.

testing.step: Rebuild the major-incident population independently
actions: Pull the auditor's own extract of incidents classified major in the financial year rather than accepting the locked population.
Cross-check against the regulatory notifications filed with the competent authority during the year and against the incidents reported to the board.
Investigate every incident present in one source and absent from another, including incidents reclassified after the year end.
Sign the reconciled test population with extract timestamps.
testing.done: an independently rebuilt major-incident population reconciles to regulatory notifications and board reporting, with all differences investigated.

testing.step: Test cost worksheet coverage across the population
actions: Match each incident in the test population to a cost worksheet and list every incident with none as an automatic exception.
Check the worksheet completion date against the incident closure date to identify worksheets reconstructed months later.
Confirm each worksheet covers all three blocks - direct costs, indirect losses and recoveries - rather than only the invoices that were easy to find.
Compute worksheet coverage as a percentage and compare it to the figure reported monthly to the CISO.
testing.done: every major incident is matched to a complete worksheet or logged as an exception, with reconstruction lags identified.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of incidents and cost lines
actions: Take 100 percent of the five largest incidents by gross cost and 100 percent of incidents affecting a critical or important function.
Take 15 further incidents at random using a recorded seed, plus 30 individual cost lines selected across categories.
Include at least 5 lines that are estimated rather than booked, since those carry the method risk.
Record population size, seed and selection date for reproducibility.
testing.done: the sample covers the largest and CIF-affecting incidents plus a reproducible selection of booked and estimated cost lines.

testing.step: Vouch sampled cost lines to source documents
actions: For each sampled booked line open the ledger document and confirm the amount, the date, the vendor and the incident reference agree with the worksheet.
For apportioned invoices recompute the apportionment on the stated basis and confirm the split reaches the invoice total across all incidents.
For internal labour recompute hours times the agreed rate against the time recording data.
Log every difference, including amounts booked in the wrong financial year.
testing.done: every sampled booked line is vouched to a ledger document or timesheet, with apportionments recomputed to the invoice total.

testing.step: Challenge the estimation method on estimated components
actions: Read the method note and independently recompute the business interruption estimate for the largest incident from the outage window and the transaction volume data.
Test the sensitivity by re-running the aggregate with the two largest assumptions moved to their reasonable bounds and record the range.
Confirm the method was CFO-approved before the figure was locked and that any change from the prior year was disclosed and restated.
Log estimated amounts presented without a stated method or basis as exceptions.
testing.done: the largest estimated component is independently recomputed, the aggregate sensitivity range is stated and undocumented estimates are logged.

testing.step: Re-perform the ledger and loss database reconciliations
actions: Pull the ICT incident cost centre, provision and recovery postings directly from the ERP for the financial year.
Rebuild the reconciliation to the aggregate and confirm each reconciling item is supported rather than described.
Rebuild the reconciliation to the operational risk loss database and test that definitional differences are stated and quantified.
Compute the unexplained difference and compare it to the agreed materiality threshold.
testing.done: both reconciliations are rebuilt from source extracts and the unexplained difference is computed against the materiality threshold.

testing.step: Test recovery treatment and presentation
actions: For each sampled recovery trace to the insurance settlement advice, the claim record or the provider credit note.
Confirm receivable recoveries are shown separately from received recoveries and are not netted into the gross cost line.
Check that service credits the entity paid out were treated as losses and not offset against credits received.
Recompute gross, recoveries and net totals from the per-incident schedule and agree them to the certified figures.
testing.done: every sampled recovery is traced to a settlement document and gross, recovery and net totals recompute to the certified figures.

testing.step: Test the certification and the Art. 6(5) framework review evidence
actions: Read the signed certification and confirm it names the financial year, the figures, the population and the method version, and carries both executive signatures.
Recompute the days from year end to signature against the 90-day internal deadline.
Confirm the framework review record shows an annual review and a separate review after each major incident in the year, each with a date and an outcome.
Trace the management body noting to the board minutes and confirm the figure minuted matches the certified figure.
testing.done: the certification is complete and timely, and the framework review record evidences both the annual and the post-incident reviews.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and correction date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the incident or cost line affected and the Art. 11(10) or Art. 6(5) consequence.

Assign a root cause from the list - worksheet not completed at closure, cost not tagged to the incident, apportionment undocumented, method not approved, reconciliation unexplained, certification late, post-incident framework review not recorded.
Name an owner across Security Operations, Operational Risk and Finance and set a correction date before the next cycle opens.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a coded root cause, an owner in the right function, a correction date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Summarise worksheet coverage, unexplained reconciling difference against materiality, the sensitivity range on the aggregate and the days to certification.
State a conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - against the full-coverage, within-materiality and 90-day thresholds.
Have the reviewer, who prepared no worksheet, reconciliation or certification, sign the workpaper with name and date.
Report to the audit committee and file the signed workpaper under DORA/Art-11-10 in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper carries coverage, reconciliation and timeliness statistics, a stated conclusion and a recorded committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns oversight of ICT third-party providers designated critical by the ESAs - tracking the Lead Overseer's recommendations, assessing the risk where a provider does not endorse them, and driving suspension or termination where the risk cannot be managed; escalates to the Chief Info Security Officer and the management body

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Arts. 31-42 on the oversight framework for critical ICT third-party service providers, in particular Art. 42 on the use of designated providers and the treatment of non-endorsed recommendations, read with Art. 28(2) and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1773 and with Art. 26(1)-(2) on threat-led penetration testing; checked on EUR-Lex whenever the ESAs update the register of designated providers

In-scope processes.value: Monitoring the ESA register of designated critical ICT third-party providers -> mapping designations onto the firm's own arrangements -> tracking Lead Overseer recommendations and the provider's endorsement position -> assessing and managing the residual risk of non-endorsement -> exit strategy readiness -> suspension or termination decision where required -> notification to the competent authority and the supporting exit execution

In-scope systems.value: The CLM repository holds the contracts, termination rights and exit clauses; the Register of Information identifies which arrangements involve a designated provider and which support a critical or important function; the GRC platform holds the risk assessments, the recommendation tracker and the exit plan status

Compliance procedure documented.value: Critical ICT Provider Oversight Procedure - ESA register monitoring cadence, the mapping rule from designation to affected arrangements, the recommendation intake and tracking method, the non-endorsement risk assessment template, exit strategy and transition plan standards, and the suspension and termination decision protocol with its notification steps

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Risk Officer under the management-body-approved ICT third-party policy; re-approved whenever the ESAs designate new providers, publish oversight guidance, or the competent authority issues a direction on a provider the firm uses

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: ESA register of designated providers checked at least monthly and on any public designation announcement; each Lead Overseer recommendation assessed within 30 days of becoming known, with the provider's endorsement position confirmed after the 60-day window it has to respond; exit plans for designated-provider CIF arrangements tested at least annually; any competent authority direction to suspend or terminate actioned inside the deadline the authority sets

Deadline reminders configured.value: GRC platform holds a monthly ESA register check task, a 30-day assessment clock on each new recommendation, a 60-day follow-up to confirm the provider's endorsement position, an annual exit-test task per designated-provider CIF arrangement, and contract notice-period alerts at 180, 120 and 60 days before each renewal or break date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Register checks, designation mapping, recommendation records with the provider's endorsement position, risk assessments, board and committee decisions, exit plans and test results, and any suspension or termination correspondence retained 5 years from the end of the arrangement and produced to the competent authority or Lead Overseer on request

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A designation not mapped to the affected arrangements, a recommendation not assessed inside 30 days, continued use of a provider that refused a recommendation with no documented risk decision, a CIF arrangement with no tested exit plan, and a missed competent authority direction are each logged as an issue with an executive owner and a board-reported date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The CRO signs every decision to continue using a designated provider that has not endorsed a Lead Overseer recommendation, naming the residual risk, the compensating measures and the review date

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All contractual arrangements with providers on the ESA register of designated critical ICT third-party providers, all Lead Overseer recommendations known in the period, all non-endorsement risk assessments, and all exit plans for designated-provider arrangements supporting a critical or important function

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Fail if a designated provider used by the firm was not identified within 30 days of designation, if a recommendation went unassessed beyond 30 days, if the firm continued to use a provider that declined a recommendation without a CRO-signed risk decision, if any designated-provider CIF arrangement has no exit plan tested in the last 12 months, or if a competent authority direction was actioned late; every one of these is reported to the management body

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is event-driven on designations and recommendations and annual on exit testing, so assurance runs quarterly over the designation and recommendation population and annually over exit plans and the full designated-provider portfolio

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: The auditor must not have performed any sampled risk assessment, exit test or contract negotiation, and must source the ESA designation list independently of the vendor management team

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly critical ICT provider oversight workpaper - designation mapping reconciliation, recommendation tracker re-performance, risk decision review, exit plan testing evidence and exception log - in the compliance evidence repository under DORA/Arts-31-42

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The designated-provider portfolio with affected critical or important functions, the recommendation tracker with endorsement positions, the CRO-signed risk decisions, exit plans with their latest test results and the board minutes, producible to the competent authority or the Lead Overseer within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Third-Party Risk Manager assembles the response, the Chief Risk Officer owns the dialogue with the competent authority on continued use of a designated provider, and Legal Counsel clears any correspondence touching suspension, termination or a dispute with the provider

checklist.step: Monitor the ESA register of designated critical ICT providers
actions: Check the ESAs' published register of designated critical ICT third-party service providers monthly and on any designation announcement, recording the check date even when nothing changed.
Capture for each designation the provider's legal name, LEI, the designating decision date and the Lead Overseer appointed (EBA, EIOPA or ESMA).
Watch for a provider opting in voluntarily under Art. 31(11) as well as being designated, since both bring the arrangement into scope.
Circulate every change to the Third-Party Risk Manager and the Chief Info Security Officer within 2 business days.
checklist.done: a dated monthly register check exists with every designation captured by provider LEI, decision date and Lead Overseer, and circulated within 2 business days.

checklist.step: Map each designation onto the firm's own arrangements
actions: Match the designated provider's LEI against the Register of Information provider list, including matches at group-parent and subsidiary level.
Extend the match into the subcontracting chains - a designated provider sitting at rank 2 or 3 behind a direct supplier still brings the arrangement into scope.
List for each match the contracts affected, the critical or important functions they support, the annual spend and the contract renewal or break date.
Open a designated-provider record in the GRC platform for each match with the Vendor Manager named as relationship owner.
Report the mapped portfolio to the Chief Info Security Officer within 30 days of the designation.
checklist.done: every designation is mapped within 30 days to the affected contracts and functions, including matches found inside subcontracting chains.

checklist.step: Establish the intake route for Lead Overseer recommendations
actions: Ask each designated provider in writing to notify the firm of recommendations addressed to it by its Lead Overseer and of its endorsement position.
Add the notification obligation to the contract at the next amendment window through the Contracts Manager where it is not already there.
Supplement provider notification with the firm's own monitoring of ESA and competent authority publications, since the provider's disclosure cannot be the only source.
Record each recommendation as it becomes known with its date, subject matter and the affected service domain.
checklist.done: a written notification obligation is in place with each designated provider and every known recommendation is logged with its date and subject.

checklist.step: Assess each recommendation's relevance to the firm within 30 days
actions: Read the recommendation and identify whether it touches the specific service the firm consumes rather than the provider's business generally.
Assess what it means for the critical or important functions the service supports - the risk the Lead Overseer identified is a risk the firm now carries.
Record the assessment against the designated-provider record with a relevance conclusion, the functions affected and the officer who reached it, inside 30 days of the recommendation becoming known.
Where relevant, raise a monitoring action to track the provider's remediation and set a review date.
checklist.done: each recommendation has a dated relevance assessment inside 30 days naming the affected functions and a tracked monitoring action where relevant.

checklist.step: Confirm the provider's endorsement position after its response window
actions: Ask the provider in writing, after the 60-day window it has to respond to its Lead Overseer, whether it endorsed the recommendation or gave a reasoned explanation for not doing so.
Obtain the reasoned explanation itself where the provider declined, not merely a summary of it.
Record the position - endorsed, endorsed with conditions, declined, or no response - on the designated-provider record with the evidence attached.
Treat a provider that will not disclose its position as a declined position for risk purposes and say so on the record.
checklist.done: each recommendation carries a documented provider endorsement position with the underlying correspondence, and non-disclosure is treated as declined.

checklist.step: Assess and manage the risk where a recommendation is not endorsed
actions: Build the risk assessment on what the unaddressed weakness means for the firm's own critical or important functions, using the Lead Overseer's stated concern as the starting point.
Consider substitutability of the provider, concentration across the group, the notice period and the realistic transition time from the exit plan.
Set compensating measures the firm can apply itself - additional monitoring, contractual controls, architectural changes, data replication outside the provider - with owners and dates.
Present the assessment with a recommendation to continue, continue with measures, reduce reliance, or exit, and route it to the Chief Risk Officer.
Record the residual risk on the ICT risk register with a review date no more than 6 months away.
checklist.done: each non-endorsement has a written risk assessment with compensating measures, a recommended course of action and a residual risk entry with a review date.

checklist.step: Take the continue-or-exit decision at executive level
actions: Review the assessment with the Chief Info Security Officer, the General Counsel and the business owner of the affected function.
Decide and sign - continue with stated measures, reduce dependency to a stated level by a stated date, or terminate the arrangement.
State explicitly why continued use is acceptable where that is the decision, because Art. 42 requires the firm to manage the risk of non-endorsement rather than absorb it silently.
Refer any decision affecting a critical or important function to the management body for approval and record the minute reference.
Set a mandatory reassessment date and diary it in the GRC platform.
checklist.done: a signed executive decision states the course of action, the reasoning, the board reference where required and a diarised reassessment date.

checklist.step: Keep exit strategies real and transition plans current
actions: For each designated-provider CIF arrangement maintain an exit plan naming the trigger events, the alternative provider or in-house option, the data extraction method and format, the transition duration and the cost.

Check the contract carries the exit assistance obligations, the data return and deletion terms and the transition period the plan assumes - a plan that outruns the contractual notice period is not a plan.
Confirm the alternative option is actually available at the required scale, testing it with the alternative provider rather than assuming market capacity.
Update the plan whenever the architecture, the volume or the contract changes, and record the update date.
checklist.done: every designated-provider CIF arrangement has a current exit plan whose transition assumptions are supported by contract terms and a verified alternative.

checklist.step: Test the exit plan at least annually
actions: Run an annual exit test for each designated-provider CIF arrangement - at minimum a data extraction rehearsal proving the firm can retrieve its data in a usable format within the planned window.
For the highest-dependency arrangement run a fuller transition simulation with the Enterprise Architect and the alternative provider covering integration, data mapping and cutover sequencing.
Time each step and compare it against the plan's stated transition duration, revising the plan where reality is slower.
Raise a GRC finding for every gap the test exposes, with an owner and a date, and report the test outcome to the risk committee.
checklist.done: each designated-provider CIF arrangement has a dated annual exit test with timings compared to the plan and gaps raised as owned findings.

checklist.step: Track concentration across designated providers
actions: Build the concentration view from the Register of Information - functions per provider, providers per function, and the entities across the group sharing the same provider.
Identify where several critical or important functions rest on one designated provider, or where nominally different providers share the same rank-2 subcontractor.
Set an appetite threshold with the Chief Risk Officer and report breaches with the mitigation proposed.
Feed the concentration picture into sourcing decisions before the next renewal rather than after it.
checklist.done: the concentration dashboard shows functions per designated provider and shared subcontractors, with appetite breaches reported and mitigated.

checklist.step: Act on a competent authority direction to suspend or terminate
actions: Log the direction with its date, its precise scope - whole or partial suspension, or termination - and the deadline the authority set.
Convene the Chief Risk Officer, the Chief Info Security Officer and the affected business owner within 1 business day to activate the exit or suspension plan.
Give contractual notice in the form and to the address the contract requires, and record proof of service.
Report progress to the competent authority at the interval it requires and confirm completion in writing with evidence.
Manage the continuity of the affected critical or important function through the transition and report service impact daily to the management body.
checklist.done: the direction is logged, the exit or suspension is activated within 1 business day, notice is served with proof and completion is confirmed to the authority.

checklist.step: Refresh due diligence and assurance on designated providers annually
actions: Collect each designated provider's current assurance reports, certifications and penetration test summaries covering the consumed service, and read the exceptions section rather than the opinion alone.
Confirm the provider still meets the contractual security and resilience commitments, taking service level performance from the Vendor Coordinator.
Test the provider's subcontracting position for change and require prior consent where the ICT third-party policy demands it.
Record the annual assessment outcome on the designated-provider record and escalate any deterioration to the Chief Risk Officer.
checklist.done: each designated provider has a dated annual assessment covering assurance exceptions, service level performance and subcontracting changes.

checklist.step: Support threat-led penetration testing that includes the provider
actions: Where the authority has identified the firm for threat-led penetration testing under Art. 26, scope the test to include the critical or important functions the designated provider supports.
Secure the provider's participation using the contractual testing rights, agreeing scope, rules of engagement and the handling of pooled testing where the provider offers it.
Confirm the testers meet the requirements set for TLPT and that the authority's process for validating the test is followed.
Feed the findings that concern the provider into the recommendation tracker and the annual assessment.
checklist.done: TLPT scope covers the designated provider's contribution to CIF services with the provider's participation secured contractually and findings tracked.

checklist.step: Report designated-provider oversight to the management body
actions: Report quarterly - designated providers used, functions dependent on each, open recommendations and endorsement positions, risk decisions taken, exit plan test status and concentration breaches.
Name any provider that declined a recommendation and state why continued use remains acceptable, or what is being done about it.
Ask the board to approve any continuation decision affecting a critical or important function and minute the decision.
Carry the board's directions into the sourcing and exit plans.
checklist.done: quarterly reporting covers designations, recommendations, risk decisions and exit readiness, with board approval minuted for CIF continuations.

checklist.step: File the oversight evidence pack
actions: Assemble the pack - register checks, designation mapping, recommendation tracker with endorsement evidence, risk assessments and CRO decisions, exit plans and test results, board minutes and any authority correspondence.
File under DORA/Arts-31-42/<year> with the 5-year retention label running from the end of the arrangement.
Index by provider LEI, affected function and recommendation reference so a Lead Overseer question about one provider is answerable directly.
Record the pack location on the DORA obligation record for the 5 business day production service level.
checklist.done: the oversight pack is filed, retention-labelled and indexed by provider LEI, function and recommendation reference.

testing.step: Rebuild the designated-provider portfolio independently
actions: Take the ESAs' published register of designated critical ICT third-party providers directly rather than the vendor team's copy, as at the test date and at each quarter end in the period.
Match the designated LEIs against the Register of Information provider list and against the CLM vendor master, including group subsidiaries.
Search the subcontracting chains for designated providers appearing at rank 2 or below.
Compare the auditor's portfolio to management's mapped portfolio and investigate every difference in both directions.
testing.done: an independently rebuilt designated-provider portfolio, including subcontracting-chain matches, reconciles to management's mapping.

testing.step: Recompute the designation-to-mapping response time
actions: For each designation in the period compute days between the ESA decision date and the date the firm opened its designated-provider record.
Flag every mapping beyond 30 days and every designation never mapped as exceptions.
Check the monthly register-check evidence exists for each month, including months with no change.
Confirm circulation to the CISO happened within 2 business days from the email or ticket record, not from an assertion.
testing.done: mapping response times are recomputed against the 30-day rule and monthly register checks are evidenced for every month in the period.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of arrangements and recommendations
actions: Take 100 percent of designated-provider arrangements supporting a critical or important function and 100 percent of recommendations the provider declined.
Take 10 further arrangements and 10 further recommendations at random using a recorded seed.
Include every arrangement where the firm decided to continue after a non-endorsement, since that is where the Art. 42 risk sits.
Record population size, seed and selection date for reproducibility.
testing.done: the sample covers all CIF designated-provider arrangements and all declined recommendations plus a reproducible random selection.

testing.step: Re-perform the relevance assessment on sampled recommendations
actions: Read each sampled recommendation and the service description in the contract and reach an independent view on whether it touches the service the firm consumes.
Compare to management's relevance conclusion and treat a relevant recommendation assessed as not relevant as a reportable exception.
Recompute days from the recommendation becoming known to the assessment date against the 30-day rule.
Confirm the assessment named the affected critical or important functions rather than stopping at the provider level.
testing.done: each sampled recommendation has an independent relevance view, a recomputed assessment lag and a check that affected functions were named.

testing.step: Trace endorsement positions to provider correspondence
actions: For each sampled recommendation open the recorded endorsement position and trace it to the provider's own written statement.
Where the provider declined, confirm the reasoned explanation itself is on file rather than a summary of it.
Confirm non-disclosure was recorded as a declined position rather than left blank or pending.
Check the follow-up occurred after the provider's 60-day response window rather than before it, so the position recorded is final.
testing.done: every sampled endorsement position traces to provider correspondence obtained after the 60-day window, with declined explanations on file.

testing.step: Test the risk decision behind every continued use after non-endorsement
actions: For each continuation decision confirm a written risk assessment exists, addresses the specific weakness the Lead Overseer identified, and pre-dates the decision.
Confirm the compensating measures were actually implemented by tracing each to its GRC action closure evidence rather than to the plan.
Confirm the Chief Risk Officer signature is present and, where a critical or important function is affected, that the management body approved it in the minutes.
Check the diarised reassessment date exists and has not passed unactioned.
testing.done: every continuation decision is supported by a pre-dated risk assessment, implemented measures traced to closure, and the required signatures and minutes.

testing.step: Test exit plan currency and the annual exit test
actions: For each sampled CIF arrangement confirm an exit plan exists, names a specific alternative and states a transition duration and cost.
Compare the plan's transition duration to the contractual notice period and exit assistance terms in the CLM record and flag any plan the contract cannot support.
Confirm an exit test occurred in the last 12 months and read the timings against the plan's assumptions.
Where the plan relies on an alternative provider, check the evidence that the alternative was actually approached and can take the volume.
testing.done: every sampled exit plan is current, contractually supportable, tested inside 12 months and evidenced against a verified alternative.

testing.step: Test the response to any authority direction and to concentration breaches
actions: List every competent authority direction, request or observation on designated providers received in the period.
For each, recompute days from receipt to the firm's action and to its confirmation back to the authority against the deadline set.
Trace concentration appetite breaches to a reported mitigation and confirm it moved beyond a plan into a change.
Log any direction actioned late, or any breach reported without mitigation, as an exception.
testing.done: every authority direction has recomputed response timing against its deadline and every concentration breach traces to an implemented mitigation.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the provider, the arrangement and the Art. 42 or Art. 28 element missed.

Assign a root cause from the list - register not monitored, designation not mapped through the chain, recommendation intake absent from contract, assessment late, risk decision unsigned, measures not implemented, exit plan untested, direction actioned late.
Name an executive owner and a remediation date, and require any continued use without a signed risk decision to be reported to the management body at its next sitting.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a coded root cause, an executive owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Summarise designations mapped inside 30 days, recommendations assessed inside 30 days, continuations without a signed risk decision, and CIF arrangements without a tested exit plan.
State a conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - against the zero-unmapped-designation and zero-unsigned-continuation thresholds.
Have the reviewer, who performed none of the sampled assessments, exit tests or negotiations, sign the workpaper with name and date.
Report to the risk committee and the management body and file the signed workpaper under DORA/Arts-31-42 in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper carries the mapping, assessment and exit-readiness statistics, a stated conclusion and a recorded committee reporting date.
